{"edits": [{"finding_ids": ["app/api_errors.py:10:validator"], "search": "    "field required": "MISSING",
    "value is not a valid integer": "NOT_AN_INTEGER",
    "ensure this value has at least": "TOO_SHORT",", "replace": "    "Field required": "MISSING",
    "Input should be a valid integer": "NOT_AN_INTEGER",
    "String should have at least": "TOO_SHORT",", "explanation": "The test failure is caused by the error-message lookup, not the validator. Pydantic v2 changed its built-in error messages: missing fields report "Field required" (capital F), integer parsing reports "Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer", and min_length reports "String should have at least N characters". The v1 strings in MESSAGE_CODES never match under v2, so every error fell through to the "INVALID" default. Updating the keys to the v2 message prefixes restores the intended codes (MISSING, NOT_AN_INTEGER, TOO_SHORT) while keeping the same startswith matching logic. The field_validator migration from the previous attempt is correct and is left unchanged."}], "notes": "The previous attempt's @field_validator/@classmethod migration is correct and is kept as-is. The failing test is caused by MESSAGE_CODES still using Pydantic v1 error message strings. Pydantic v2 messages differ ("Field required", "Input should be a valid integer...", "String should have at least..."), so every error fell back to "INVALID". The single edit updates those three message prefixes to their v2 equivalents. No other changes are needed: Field(..., min_length=3) and the ValidationError/errors() usage are already v2-compatible. Caveat: this is validated by reasoning about Pydantic v2 message text, not by running the test; if a message prefix differs in the installed Pydantic minor version, matching on err["type"] (e.g. "missing", "int_parsing", "string_too_short") would be more robust."}
